history.period: Construction initiated 1939 CE; disrupted during WWII (1942-1946); completed post-war
history.summary: SOLID IDENTIFICATION: the CSV's 'Kolasib Vishnu Temple' is the Lakshmi Narayan Mandir at Chanmari West, Kolasib (PIN 796081), dedicated to Vishnu (Narayan) and Lakshmi. inheritage.foundation documents it as a hilltop temple with a Nagara-style shikhara, a pillared mandapa with Mizo-influenced geometric painting, and the Lakshmi-Narayan pair in the garbhagriha (Lakshmi standing beside Vishnu in North Indian fashion). Construction was initiated in 1939, slowed during WWII (1942-1946), and completed after the war, making it one of the earliest prominent Hindu mandirs in Mizoram; the page attributes patronage to the Birla family, though its own narrative also cautions that the exact construction date is 'elusive within readily available records' - that conflict is flagged here. hinduvism.com's Mizoram top-10 list independently confirms a Lakshmi Narayan Mandir in Kolasib dedicated to Vishnu and Lakshmi, visited at Diwali and Janmashtami. Coordinates 24.30559, 92.03788 are from the inheritage page. Note: onefivenine's Kolasib District tourism page separately names 'kolasib shiv mandir' as the district's famous temple - that is a different shrine (see the Kolasib Shiva Temple record), not this one.

name: Kolasib Vishnu Temple
town_description: Kolasib is the district headquarters of Kolasib district in northern Mizoram, about 66 km south of Aizawl on NH 54 (PIN 796081). A market and transport town on the Aizawl-Assam route, it is overwhelmingly Christian (Mizo Presbyterian majority), with a small Hindu minority - mostly non-Mizo traders, government staff and paramilitary personnel - that maintains the town's few community temples. The Lakshmi Narayan Mandir stands on a hill at Chanmari West overlooking the town.
